title: INTERPRETABLE EMBEDDINGS WITH SPARSE AUTOENCODERS: A DATA ANALYSIS TOOLKIT

bias_targets.methodology: Computing the Normalized Pointwise Mutual Information (NPMI) between Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) latents representing race (e.g., Black, white people) and latents representing offensive language to find unexpected co-occurrences in datasets like CivilComments.
Computing the NPMI between SAE latents representing gender (e.g., feminine references, women) and latents representing offensive language to identify spurious correlations in text corpora.
Computing the NPMI between SAE latents representing religion or secularism (e.g., atheism) and latents representing offensive requests or language.

Analyzing the co-occurrence (via NPMI) of SAE latents representing political figures or ideologies (e.g., conservatism) with latents representing sarcastic, offensive, or specific academic/stylistic tones.
